question: Which cells in the islets of Langerhans are responsible for producing insulin?
explanation: Beta cells within the islets of Langerhans are responsible for the secretion of insulin, which helps lower blood glucose levels. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T7#GNS222_U2_T7_h1)

question: Why are pancreatic exocrine enzymes primarily secreted in inactive forms (zymogens)?

options.A: To accelerate absorption in the stomach
options.B: To prevent self-digestion of the pancreatic tissue
options.C: To bind with circulating glucose molecules
options.D: To stimulate alpha cell hormone release

explanation: Enzymes are released in inactive zymogen forms to protect the pancreas from digesting its own structural tissues. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T7#GNS222_U2_T7_h1)

question: What are the two most common causes of acute pancreatitis?

options.B: Viral hepatitis and peptic ulcer disease
options.C: High sodium intake and sedentary lifestyle

explanation: Gallstones obstructing the biliary tract and chronic heavy alcohol use are the leading causes of acute pancreatitis. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T7#GNS222_U2_T7_h2)

question: Which clinical sign indicates retroperitoneal bleeding in severe acute pancreatitis?
explanation: Cullen's sign (periumbilical bruising) and Grey Turner's sign (flank bruising) are indicators of severe hemorrhagic pancreatitis. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T7#GNS222_U2_T7_h2)

question: What is a hallmark manifestation of exocrine insufficiency in chronic pancreatitis?
explanation: Steatorrhea, characterized by fatty, foul-smelling stools, occurs due to the impaired digestion and absorption of fats from exocrine failure. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T7#GNS222_U2_T7_h3)

question: How does chronic pancreatitis fundamentally differ from acute pancreatitis in terms of pathology?

options.A: It causes temporary inflammation without tissue damage
options.B: It results in permanent, irreversible fibrosis and destruction
options.C: It exclusively affects endocrine islet cells
options.D: It is never caused by alcohol consumption

explanation: Chronic pancreatitis causes permanent anatomical changes, including irreversible fibrosis, strictures, and destruction of both exocrine and endocrine tissue. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T7#GNS222_U2_T7_h3)

question: Which blood test is considered more specific for diagnosing acute pancreatitis than amylase?
explanation: Serum lipase is more specific to pancreatic injury and stays elevated longer than amylase during acute pancreatitis. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T7#GNS222_U2_T7_h4)

question: What is regarded as the gold standard imaging modality for diagnosing acute pancreatitis and assessing necrosis?
explanation: A contrast-enhanced CT scan is the gold standard for visualizing pancreatic inflammation, necrosis, and structural complications. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T7#GNS222_U2_T7_h4)

question: What is the primary rationale for administering intravenous fluids aggressively in early acute pancreatitis?

options.B: To prevent hypovolemic shock and maintain organ perfusion
options.C: To stimulate the release of insulin from beta cells
options.D: To flush gallstones out of the common bile duct

explanation: Aggressive fluid resuscitation is critical to offset third-spacing and systemic inflammation, preventing hypovolemic shock and maintaining organ perfusion. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T7#GNS222_U2_T7_h5)

question: When should pancreatic enzyme replacement therapy (PERT) be administered to a patient with chronic pancreatitis?

options.C: Once daily on an empty stomach
options.D: Only when severe abdominal pain occurs

explanation: PERT must be taken with every meal and snack to adequately mix with food and assist in digesting fats, proteins, and carbohydrates. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T7#GNS222_U2_T7_h5)

question: Why is pancreatic cancer often diagnosed at an advanced stage?

options.A: It spreads exclusively through the lymphatic system
options.B: Early symptoms are often insidious and vague
options.C: Routine screening blood tests detect it immediately
options.D: Tumors never cause any physical symptoms

explanation: Pancreatic cancer presents insidiously with vague symptoms in early stages, leading to late diagnosis when the disease is advanced. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T7#GNS222_U2_T7_h6)

question: What classic clinical manifestation is typically seen early in patients with a tumor located in the head of the pancreas?
explanation: Tumors in the head of the pancreas obstruct the common bile duct early on, resulting in painless jaundice, dark urine, and pale stools. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T7#GNS222_U2_T7_h6)

question: What is the name of the complex surgical procedure performed for resectable tumors in the head of the pancreas?
explanation: The Whipple procedure (pancreaticoduodenectomy) is the standard surgical resection for tumors located in the head of the pancreas. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T7#GNS222_U2_T7_h7)

question: What is the primary goal of medical and oncological management for patients with metastatic pancreatic cancer?

options.C: Palliation and enhancement of quality of life

explanation: When pancreatic cancer is metastatic and unresectable, management focuses on palliation, pain control, and improving quality of life. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T7#GNS222_U2_T7_h7)

question: What is a major complication following pancreatic surgery characterized by the leakage of fluid from surgical anastomoses?
explanation: A pancreatic fistula is a common and serious postoperative complication involving the leakage of pancreatic secretions from the anastomotic site. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T7#GNS222_U2_T7_h8)

question: What is a key nursing responsibility when caring for surgical drains following a Whipple procedure?

options.A: Flushing the drains with sterile water every hour
options.B: Monitoring and recording drain output volume, color, and consistency
options.C: Removing the drains on the first postoperative day
options.D: Clamping the drains continuously to prevent fluid loss

explanation: Nurses must closely monitor and record drain output characteristics to detect early complications like hemorrhage or anastomotic leaks. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T7#GNS222_U2_T7_h8)
